resourceProfile.assessment: The complete English and French source scope, review metadata, glossary, and project concept references were available locally.

automatedQuality.summary: Translation review metadata, queue validation, typecheck, 79 test files with 462 tests, complete build, 39 IIS rules with 61 route cases, and 724 generated-link checks passed.

linguisticCritique.summary: A bounded French pass identified 25 actionable defects in electrical, circuit, trigonometric, thermal, and unit terminology; all 25 were corrected.

competentHumanReview.summary: No competent French human review was performed in this cycle; changed IDs remain machine-drafted.

publicationAuthorization.summary: No merge, publication, deployment, or residual-risk authorization was requested or granted.

findings.summary: The resistance-example title used an incorrect French construction.
evidence: The previous title was ‘Trouver de la résistance’.

findings.summary: The resistance formula contained the corrupted result ‘6 = 9’.
evidence: The previous expression was ‘R = 12 V / 2 A = 6 = 9’.

findings.summary: The resistance conclusion repeated the corrupted result.
evidence: The previous conclusion ended with ‘6 = 9’.

findings.summary: Electrical power was translated as electrical energy.
evidence: The section formula and paragraph describe puissance P, not energy.

findings.summary: The Joule-heating summary said current transforms resistance into heat.
evidence: Electrical energy, not resistance, is converted into heat.
findings.resolution: Rephrased it as electrical current transforming electrical energy into heat.

findings.summary: The Joule formula used spaces inside superscript expressions.
evidence: The previous expression was ‘P = I ^ 2 × R = 3 ^ 2’.
findings.resolution: Restored the protected formula syntax I^2 and 3^2.

findings.summary: The paragraph called electrical energy a rate of transfer.
evidence: The source distinguishes power as a rate from energy itself.
findings.resolution: Changed the subject to puissance électrique.

findings.summary: The circuit introduction used an awkward literal phrase for reasoning about a diagram.
evidence: The previous text said the terms made reasoning about a schematic easier.
findings.resolution: Changed it to facilitate understanding a circuit schematic.

findings.summary: A branch was translated as an ‘actual’ path instead of a current path.
evidence: The previous text used ‘chemin actuel’.

findings.summary: The current-law title used ‘actuelle’ rather than the electrical-current term.
evidence: The previous title was ‘La loi actuelle de Kirchhoff’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘La loi des courants de Kirchhoff’.

findings.summary: The parallel-branches formula retained English text.
evidence: The previous expression ended with ‘parallel branches’.

findings.summary: The series formula retained English text.
evidence: The previous expression ended with ‘series’.

findings.summary: The parallel formula retained English text.
evidence: The previous expression ended with ‘parallel’.

findings.summary: The sine formula retained English geometry terms.
evidence: The previous expression used ‘opposite / hypotenuse’.

findings.summary: The cosine formula retained English geometry terms.
evidence: The previous expression used ‘adjacent / hypotenuse’.

findings.summary: The tangent formula retained English geometry terms.
evidence: The previous expression used ‘opposite / adjacent’.

findings.summary: The opposite-side formula used an awkward literal phrase.
evidence: The previous expression began with ‘ci-contre’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the technical term ‘opposé’.

findings.summary: The adjacent-side formula retained English text.
evidence: The previous expression used ‘adjacent’ in an otherwise French example.
findings.resolution: Retained the standard French technical term ‘adjacent’.

findings.summary: The waveform note mistranslated sign as panel.
evidence: The previous text said ‘Gardez le panneau’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to preserve the sign and quadrant.

findings.summary: The heat-capacity summary used incorrect French question grammar.
evidence: The previous text said ‘Quelle quantité d’énergie un objet a besoin’.
findings.resolution: Rephrased it as ‘De quelle quantité d'énergie un objet a-t-il besoin’.

findings.summary: The water example title was an unnatural noun phrase.
evidence: The previous title was ‘Eau de chauffage’.

findings.summary: The heat-capacity conclusion referred to a radiator instead of a heater.
evidence: The source discusses a real heater; ‘radiateur’ narrows the meaning incorrectly.

findings.summary: The heat-flux check used an infinitive instead of an imperative.
evidence: The previous bullet began ‘Distinguer’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the formal imperative ‘Distinguez’.

findings.summary: The final heat-flux check used an infinitive instead of an imperative.
evidence: The previous bullet ended with ‘utiliser’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘utilisez’ and clarified temperature changes.

findings.summary: The SI table mistranslated mass as ‘Messe’.
evidence: The previous row used ‘Messe’ instead of ‘Masse’.
